purpose: Crosswalk between classic software design patterns and agent harness patterns, anchored in documented Claude Code mechanisms. Feeds the guide page, the landing page, and the MCP resource claude-code-guide://ai-design-patterns.
method: A crosswalk row enters only when at least one public source maps the classic pattern to an agent analogue, a documented Claude Code mechanism exists, and a failure mode can be stated. Claude Code mechanisms are checked against the official documentation at https://code.claude.com/docs/llms-full.txt. Rows marked own-synthesis are this guide's mapping to Claude Code: the sources give the generic agent analogue only.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Let a creator decide which concrete product to instantiate, behind a common interface.

agent_analogue.label: Subagent spawning from a named definition

claude_code.name: Subagent definitions and the Agent tool

crosswalk.failure_mode: The factory hands every product the full toolbox: a subagent definition without a tools field inherits every tool available to subagents.
crosswalk.verify: List the tools field of each definition in .claude/agents/ and fail review when a write-capable agent has no explicit allowlist.

infographic.alt: Factory Method card (GoF creational). Classic: A creator decides which product to build. In Claude Code: Subagent definitions and the Agent tool. Breaks when: A definition without a tools field inherits every tool. Check: Give every write-capable agent an explicit tools allowlist.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Guarantee one shared instance of a component with a global access point.

agent_analogue.label: Shared tool registry
Layered memory governance: decide which state is shared, isolated, persisted, or ephemeral

claude_code.name: CLAUDE.md hierarchy and auto memory (shared state, not a Singleton)

crosswalk.failure_mode: Claude Code provides no Singleton here: several CLAUDE.md and memory files load and combine, and nothing enforces one instance or one access point. What carries over is the risk of unmanaged shared state: parallel sessions or agents that write the same memory file at the same time can overwrite each other's entries.
crosswalk.verify: Run two sessions that both append to the same memory file and check whether either entry is lost.

related.title: Memory systems: the native Claude Code memory stack
Persistent memory: the six failures that never raise an error

infographic.alt: Singleton card (GoF creational). Classic: One shared instance with one global access point. In Claude Code: CLAUDE.md hierarchy and auto memory. Breaks when: Parallel writers to one memory file overwrite each other. Check: Append from two sessions at once and look for lost entries.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Convert the interface of an existing component into the interface a client expects.

agent_analogue.label: Tool adapter that exposes an external system to the model

crosswalk.failure_mode: The adapter mirrors every upstream endpoint, so tool definitions crowd the context and the model picks among near-duplicate tools.
crosswalk.verify: Run /mcp and /context, then remove or defer the tools that no task in the last sprint used.

related.title: MCP servers: what they actually cost and when to use them

videos.point: The speakers explain that each vendor exposes its own APIs through an MCP server layer, a unified wrapper the LLM can use.

infographic.alt: Adapter card (GoF structural). Classic: Convert one interface into the one a client expects. In Claude Code: MCP servers. Breaks when: Mirroring every endpoint crowds the context with near-duplicate tools. Check: Run /mcp and /context, then defer the tools nobody used.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Treat a single object and a tree of objects through the same interface.

agent_analogue.label: An agent that delegates to agents that can delegate again

crosswalk.failure_mode: Recursion without a budget: each layer multiplies token use. Claude Code caps nesting with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH, which can be adjusted but not removed.
crosswalk.verify: Set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH explicitly for automated runs and log spawned subagents with a SubagentStop hook.

videos.point: The speakers show an agent in a sequence that is itself a loop of two agents, so a workflow is used like a single sub agent.

infographic.alt: Composite card (GoF structural). Classic: Treat one object and a tree of objects alike. In Claude Code: Nested subagents, capped by spawn depth. Breaks when: Each nesting layer multiplies token use. Check: Set the spawn depth explicitly and log every spawned subagent.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Add behavior to an object by wrapping it, without changing its class.

agent_analogue.label: Guardrail wrapped around a model call
Context-injection middleware that enriches each request

crosswalk.failure_mode: A classic decorator stack has a fixed order. Matching hooks run in parallel, so a wrapper that assumes another wrapper already ran is a race.
crosswalk.verify: Write each hook so it passes when run alone, and test it with the other hooks disabled.

related.title: Smart-Suggest routing: a UserPromptSubmit hook that adds skill candidates to the prompt

videos.point: The speaker explains Spring AI advisors as a filter or pre-processor that wraps calls to and from the model and can mutate or log each request.
An Anthropic speaker says hooks fire as events in the Agent SDK and are used for deterministic verification or for inserting context.

infographic.alt: Decorator card (GoF structural). Classic: Add behavior by wrapping, in a fixed order. In Claude Code: UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse hooks. Breaks when: Matching hooks run in parallel, so there is no fixed order. Check: Make each hook pass when it runs alone.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Offer one simple entry point in front of a complex subsystem.

agent_analogue.label: Project instruction file as the single entry point for conventions

crosswalk.failure_mode: The facade is read as a contract. The docs state that Claude treats CLAUDE.md as context, not enforced configuration: a rule written there is a request, not a guarantee.
crosswalk.verify: For every must-never rule in CLAUDE.md, add a PreToolUse hook or a deny rule and a test that triggers it.

related.title: ctxharness: checks that claims in CLAUDE.md and rules still match the project

infographic.alt: Facade card (GoF structural). Classic: One simple entry point to a complex subsystem. In Claude Code: CLAUDE.md. Breaks when: CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration. Check: Back each must-never rule with a hook or a deny rule.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Pass a request along a chain of handlers until one of them handles it.

agent_analogue.label: Hook or permission pipeline in front of tool calls
Agents chained so each one handles what it can and passes the rest

claude_code.name: Permission rules: deny, then ask, then allow

crosswalk.failure_mode: Teams expect declaration order or rule specificity to decide. The docs state that rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow, and specificity does not change that order: a broad deny beats a narrow allow.
crosswalk.verify: Add a deny and a more specific allow for the same command in a test project and check that the command stays blocked.

infographic.alt: Chain of Responsibility card (GoF behavioral). Classic: Pass a request along handlers until one handles it. In Claude Code: Permission rules: deny, then ask, then allow. Breaks when: Specificity does not win: a broad deny beats a narrow allow. Check: Add a deny and a narrower allow, confirm the command stays blocked.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Turn a request into an object that can be queued, logged, checked, or undone.

agent_analogue.label: A tool call: a named action with structured arguments

crosswalk.failure_mode: The command object is written by the model. Without validation before dispatch, a malformed or out-of-scope argument executes as written.
crosswalk.verify: Feed a PreToolUse hook a recorded tool input with an out-of-scope path and assert that it blocks.

infographic.alt: Command card (GoF behavioral). Classic: Turn a request into an object you can queue, log or check. In Claude Code: Tool calls and PreToolUse hooks. Breaks when: The model writes the arguments, and unchecked they run as written. Check: Replay an out-of-scope tool input and assert the hook blocks it.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Centralize how a set of components talk, so they do not reference each other directly.

agent_analogue.label: Orchestrator that coordinates workers which never talk to each other

claude_code.name: Agent teams (experimental, off by default; peer messaging, the non-mediated alternative)

crosswalk.failure_mode: The topology is not enforced, and the mediator can become the bottleneck. A subagent whose tools include SendMessage can message other named agents directly, without agent teams. And if workers return transcripts instead of summaries, the coordinating context fills with material it never reads again.
crosswalk.verify: Leave SendMessage out of a worker's tools when all traffic must go through the coordinator, ask each subagent for a bounded final report, and compare /context before and after a delegation.

related.title: Cross-session messaging: peer messages without a mediator

videos.point: In orchestration, every call goes through the orchestrator and agents never call each other.

infographic.alt: Mediator card (GoF behavioral). Classic: Components talk through one coordinator. In Claude Code: The main conversation coordinating subagents. Breaks when: Workers return transcripts and flood the coordinator's context. Check: Ask each subagent for a bounded final report.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Capture an object's state so it can be restored later without exposing its internals.

agent_analogue.label: Checkpoint and rewind of agent state

crosswalk.failure_mode: The snapshot is partial. The docs state that checkpoints only track changes made through Claude's file editing tools; Bash commands and external processes are not captured, and edits made by a background subagent usually are not either.
crosswalk.verify: Use a Bash command to change a file Claude has not edited in this session, rewind, and confirm the change survives. Commit with git before risky shell work or delegated edits.

videos.point: The speaker argues agents need a save button: runtime checkpoints that let you replay, diff and decide, instead of read-only traces.

infographic.alt: Memento card (GoF behavioral). Classic: Snapshot the state and restore it later. In Claude Code: Checkpoints and /rewind. Breaks when: Only Claude's file edits are tracked, not Bash or external changes. Check: Edit a file with Bash, rewind, and the change is still there.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Notify subscribers automatically when a subject changes state.

agent_analogue.label: Lifecycle hooks that react to agent events

crosswalk.failure_mode: Subscribers assume an order. The docs state that matching hooks run in parallel, that Claude Code combines their outputs after all of them finish, and that for permission decisions the most restrictive result applies: one hook's deny does not stop a sibling hook's side effects.
crosswalk.verify: Run each hook alone against a recorded event payload; a hook that only passes after another one is not an observer.

videos.point: The speaker defines hooks as actions guaranteed to fire on agent events, such as just before a file read or when the conversation stops.

infographic.alt: Observer card (GoF behavioral). Classic: Subscribers are notified when state changes. In Claude Code: Hooks on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SubagentStop. Breaks when: Hooks that assume an order, while matching hooks run in parallel. Check: Run each hook alone on a recorded event.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Swap one algorithm for another behind the same interface at runtime.

agent_analogue.label: Model or approach selected per task
Runtime strategy switching, with the harness recording why, at what cost, and how to roll back

crosswalk.failure_mode: The strategy changes silently. Nobody can tell afterwards which model produced which result or what the switch cost.
crosswalk.verify: Pin model in each subagent definition and check /usage or the session transcript after a run.

related.title: agent-router-core: experimental deterministic routing CLI for agent workflows
cc-copilot-bridge: multi-provider routing for Claude Code
Measuring your own AI usage: three meters, three different answers

videos.point: The speaker argues that one model for every task is overkill and that routing each task to a fitting model cuts cost and risk.

infographic.alt: Strategy card (GoF behavioral). Classic: Swap the algorithm behind one interface. In Claude Code: The model field per subagent and /model. Breaks when: The model switches silently, with no record of cost or origin. Check: Pin the model per subagent and review /usage after the run.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Fix the skeleton of an algorithm and let subclasses fill in some steps.

agent_analogue.label: System prompt that defines the steps
Fixed agent-loop skeleton with pluggable steps

claude_code.name: Stop hook as the final step check

crosswalk.failure_mode: A prose skeleton is not enforced: the model can skip or reorder a step, unlike a base class that calls the steps itself.
crosswalk.verify: Give the last step an artifact (a file, a test run) and block completion with a Stop hook when the artifact is missing.

videos.point: The speaker describes Stripe's blueprints: agent skills interwoven with deterministic code in a fixed workflow.

infographic.alt: Template Method card (GoF behavioral). Classic: A fixed skeleton calls the steps. In Claude Code: Skills that define a procedure, plus a Stop hook. Breaks when: A prose skeleton is not enforced, so steps get skipped. Check: Block completion with a Stop hook when the artifact is missing.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Process a message through a sequence of independent steps connected by channels.

agent_analogue.label: Pipeline where each agent or model call is a filter

claude_code.name: Print mode in a shell pipeline (claude -p)

crosswalk.failure_mode: A filter emits free text that the next filter misreads, and the error travels down the pipe.
crosswalk.verify: Use --output-format json between steps and validate the shape before the next filter runs.

videos.point: The speaker pipes git log into claude -p to generate release notes and calls it pipes and filters all over again.
The speakers present the sequence pattern, calling one agent after another, also known as prompt chaining.

infographic.alt: Pipes and Filters card (Enterprise integration). Classic: Steps connected by channels, one after another. In Claude Code: claude -p in a shell pipeline. Breaks when: Free text from one step is misread by the next. Check: Use JSON output and validate it between steps.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Route each message to a destination based on its content.

agent_analogue.label: Classifier that sends a request to a specialized handler

crosswalk.failure_mode: Overlapping descriptions route the same request to different handlers from one run to the next.
crosswalk.verify: Keep a set of routing prompts with the expected subagent or skill, and rerun it after every description change.

image.alt: A worked Content-Based Router: the BM25 skill router, step by step. On every prompt a hook scores the text against positive and negative example prompts for each skill, and suggests up to three skills whose best positive match beats their best negative match and clears a calibrated per-skill threshold.

related.title: cc-skill-usage: counts real Skill invocations in transcripts

videos.point: Doctolib's Alfred has a route agent that uses an intention classification model to send each request to a specialized agent.
The speaker describes a router that receives a message and decides which agent gets it, by LLM or plain if and else.

infographic.alt: Content-Based Router card (Enterprise integration). Classic: Route each message by its content. In Claude Code: Delegation and skill selection by description. Breaks when: Overlapping descriptions route the same request differently. Check: Rerun a routing test set after every description change.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Send a request to several recipients and aggregate their replies.

agent_analogue.label: Parallel agents followed by a synthesis step

crosswalk.failure_mode: The gather step averages contradicting answers instead of reconciling them, and token cost grows with every branch.
crosswalk.verify: Make the synthesis step list disagreements explicitly, and compare the run's cost with a single-agent baseline.

videos.point: The speaker describes calling several agents in parallel, waiting for all results and passing them to a summarizer.
In a demo, the agent fans out 15 subagents in parallel and then picks the best result.

infographic.alt: Scatter-Gather card (Enterprise integration). Classic: Send to many recipients and aggregate the replies. In Claude Code: Parallel subagents and dynamic workflows. Breaks when: The gather step averages contradictions, and cost grows per branch. Check: List disagreements and compare cost with a single agent.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Isolate resources per consumer so one failure cannot sink the whole system.

agent_analogue.label: Per-agent isolation of context, tools, and budget

crosswalk.failure_mode: Only the context is isolated. Parallel agents still share one checkout and overwrite each other's files.
crosswalk.verify: Give write-capable parallel subagents isolation: worktree and check that git status in the main checkout stays clean during the run.

related.title: Plan-execute: running 20+ agents on a migration (worktree isolation)
wt-sweep: discovers Git worktrees and reviews integration evidence

infographic.alt: Bulkhead card (Distributed and resilience). Classic: Isolate resources so one failure cannot sink everything. In Claude Code: Subagent context isolation and worktrees. Breaks when: The context is isolated, but the checkout is shared. Check: Give parallel writers their own worktree.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Stop calling a failing dependency after repeated failures, and fail fast.

agent_analogue.label: Stop limits on turns, estimated cost, and loop depth
Breakers on tools, models, and the agent's own loop

crosswalk.failure_mode: These limits are bounded execution, not a breaker. A circuit breaker watches failures and opens; these caps are fixed before the run and do not track failures. --max-turns has no limit by default and counts turns, not cost. --max-budget-usd stops on a client-side cost estimate, and the docs warn that spend can pass the cap, so leave headroom.
crosswalk.verify: Run the automated job with --max-turns and --max-budget-usd set, on a task designed to loop, and check that it exits with an error and how far the reported spend went past the cap.

related.title: Loop & Graph Engineering: write a loop contract

videos.point: The speaker applies the circuit breaker to agent-to-agent calls: after repeated failures the circuit opens, fails fast, then half-opens to test recovery.
In a demo, an agent that exceeds its per-run budget is killed immediately, which the speaker calls a simple circuit breaker.

infographic.alt: Circuit Breaker card (Distributed and resilience). Classic: Stop calling a failing dependency and fail fast. In Claude Code: Turn and budget caps on a run. Breaks when: Static caps, often set on one layer only. Check: Run a looping task with both caps and expect an error exit.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Run a long transaction as local steps, each with a compensating action if a later step fails.

agent_analogue.label: Compensating actions for an agent plan

claude_code.name: No native saga: checkpoints plus scripted compensation

crosswalk.failure_mode: Rewind is mistaken for compensation. It restores local file edits only; a push, an API call, or a database write stays done.
crosswalk.verify: For every side-effecting step in an agent plan, write down its compensating action before the run, and test that action once.

related.title: Loop & Graph Engineering: reconcile interrupted effects before retrying

videos.point: The speaker presents the compensation or saga pattern: each agent has execute and compensate, and on failure the orchestrator walks backward calling compensate.
The speaker says a multi-step agent that fails midway must reverse the whole transaction across systems and needs a defined compensation operation.

infographic.alt: Saga card (Distributed and resilience). Classic: Local steps, each with a compensating action. In Claude Code: No native saga: checkpoints plus scripted compensation. Breaks when: Rewind undoes local edits, not a push or an API call. Check: Write and test a compensation for each side effect.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Attach cross-cutting capabilities (logging, policy, networking) next to a service instead of inside it.

agent_analogue.label: The agent harness around the model loop

claude_code.name: Hooks, permissions, and sandboxing around the loop

crosswalk.failure_mode: Policy lives in the prompt instead of the sidecar, so the model can talk itself out of it. A policy hook can also fail open: on most events, a hook that crashes or times out lets the action through unless it sets onFailure: "block".
crosswalk.verify: List each safety rule and name the layer that enforces it: hook, permission rule, sandbox, or prompt only. For each policy hook, point it at a missing script and check that the action is blocked.

related.title: Claude Code security: the attack surface few teams audit

infographic.alt: Sidecar card (Distributed and resilience). Classic: Cross-cutting policy runs next to the service. In Claude Code: Hooks, permissions and sandboxing around the loop. Breaks when: Policy in the prompt, or a hook that fails open. Check: Name the enforcing layer for every safety rule.

crosswalk.classic_intent: Store every state change as an event, and rebuild state by replaying the log.

agent_analogue.label: The trace log as the event stream of an agent run

crosswalk.failure_mode: The transcript is taken for the whole event log. It records the conversation, including model outputs and tool results, so --resume rebuilds the conversation without calling the model again. It does not record the state of files, branches, or services the session changed, so it cannot rebuild that state, and the turns after a resume are new model calls.
crosswalk.verify: Before relying on a resumed session, check that the files, branch, and services it assumes still match, and keep the state you need to rebuild in git or an explicit log.

related.title: cc-sessions: search and analyze Claude Code session history

videos.point: The speaker wants to build a coding agent harness that is purely event sourced, because the agent already keeps a log of events.
The speaker argues the log is the durable history from which every view of the agent (debugging, auditing, compaction) is a projection.

infographic.alt: Event Sourcing card (Distributed and resilience). Classic: Store every change as an event, replay to rebuild. In Claude Code: Session transcripts and --resume. Breaks when: The transcript keeps the conversation, not the files or services. Check: Check files, branch and services before trusting a resume.

native.name: Orchestrator-workers
native.summary: A central model breaks a task down at runtime, delegates the parts, and synthesizes the results.
native.why_new: Closest classic pattern: Mediator. The difference is that the model decides the decomposition during the run instead of the designer drawing it. Delegation pays on parallel work: in Google Research's controlled study, every multi-agent variant degraded a sequential planning task by 39 to 70%.

related.title: Plan-execute: running 20+ agents on a migration

videos.point: The speaker describes Factory's Missions system as an orchestrator that plans, workers that execute, and validators that verify.

infographic.alt: Orchestrator-workers card (agent-native pattern). What it does: A model splits the task at runtime, delegates, and synthesizes. In Claude Code: Subagents and dynamic workflows. What is new: The model draws the decomposition, and it pays on parallel work.

native.name: Evaluator-optimizer
native.summary: One call produces an answer, another evaluates it and sends feedback, in a loop.
native.why_new: The test oracle is itself a model, so the loop can converge on a wrong answer both sides accept.

claude_code.name: Reviewer subagent with its own context
Stop hook that runs the real tests

related.title: When an independent reviewer earns its place

videos.point: The speakers describe a generator and evaluator split into separate contexts, where the evaluator tests the result with Playwright and feeds critique back.
A separate validator role verifies the work, including end-to-end behavior, instead of only reading the code.

infographic.alt: Evaluator-optimizer card (agent-native pattern). What it does: One call answers, another evaluates and sends feedback. In Claude Code: A reviewer subagent and a Stop hook that runs the real tests. What is new: The judge is a model, so both sides can accept a wrong answer.

native.name: Plan-then-execute
native.summary: Separate a read-only planning phase from the phase that changes files.
native.why_new: The plan is a reviewable artifact written before any file changes, so a wrong approach can be caught before it costs edits. Reviewing it adds a checkpoint; it does not replace review of the code that follows, and the executing model can differ from the planning one (opusplan plans with Opus and executes with Sonnet).

related.title: Plan-execute: running 20+ agents on a migration

videos.point: The speaker plans every change in plan mode, has the AI execute the plan, then tests and commits.

infographic.alt: Plan-then-execute card (agent-native pattern). What it does: Plan read-only before any file changes. In Claude Code: Plan mode. What is new: The plan is reviewable before any edit, the code still needs review.

native.name: Context isolation
native.summary: Run a noisy side task in its own context and return a summary of the result.
native.why_new: Closest classic pattern: Bulkhead. Here the resource being protected is the context window, not threads or connections.

claude_code.name: Subagents work in their own context and report a summary

videos.point: Subagents give context isolation: each runs in its own context window and returns only its results, so the main agent's context stays clean.
The speaker names the anti-pattern of letting every subtask dump its full output into the primary thread and says to isolate subtask output instead.

infographic.alt: Context isolation card (agent-native pattern). What it does: Run a noisy side task in its own context and return a summary. In Claude Code: Subagents work in their own context and report a summary. What is new: The protected resource is the context window.

native.name: Context compaction
native.summary: Summarize the conversation when it approaches the window limit, and continue from the summary.
native.why_new: State is lossy by design: what the summary drops leaves the active context until something reloads it. Claude Code re-injects the project CLAUDE.md, auto memory, the plan, and invoked skills (capped), and re-reads up to five recent files; the rest of the conversation survives only as the summary.

related.title: Memory systems: keep history distinct from compaction

videos.point: The speakers define compaction as keeping the smallest context that can still answer the question and dropping or saving the rest.
The speaker explains that a log can grow forever while a model's view cannot, so the log must be compacted into a smaller lossy representation.

infographic.alt: Context compaction card (agent-native pattern). What it does: Summarize near the window limit and continue from the summary. In Claude Code: Auto compaction and /compact. What is new: Lossy by design: CLAUDE.md, memory and the plan reload, the rest lives in the summary.

native.name: Progressive disclosure
native.summary: Load short descriptions first and the full instructions only when they are needed.
native.why_new: Selection happens by the model reading descriptions, so a vague description hides a capability. Skills preloaded through a subagent's skills field are the exception: their full content loads at launch.

claude_code.name: Skills: descriptions at start, full content on use

videos.point: The speaker says skills brought progressive disclosure, which MCP tools lacked, and later ties Claude Code tool search to the same idea for MCP tools.

infographic.alt: Progressive disclosure card (agent-native pattern). What it does: Short descriptions first, full instructions on demand. In Claude Code: Skills and MCP tool search. What is new: A vague description hides a capability.

native.name: Deterministic gate
native.summary: Put anything that must always happen in code that runs outside the model's judgment.
native.why_new: Closest classic patterns: Sidecar and Chain of Responsibility. The difference is that the rest of the system is probabilistic, so the line between suggestion and enforcement has to be drawn on purpose.

related.title: A green review is not a merge gate
Turn recurring review comments into tested controls

videos.point: An Anthropic speaker describes a proxy layer that counts and compares, returns a 403 when a budget is crossed or a delete is attempted, and cannot be talked out of the rule by prompt injection.
The speaker uses a PreToolUse hook that blocks a tool call before it executes, turning CLAUDE.md instructions into deterministic hooks.

infographic.alt: Deterministic gate card (agent-native pattern). What it does: What must always happen runs outside the model. In Claude Code: PreToolUse hooks and deny rules. What is new: Draw the line between suggestion and enforcement on purpose.

native.name: Goal loop
native.summary: Keep the agent working until a stated completion condition is met.
native.why_new: Whether the goal is met is judged by a model, so the condition must be checkable.

videos.point: The speakers explain the Ralph loop: feed one prompt to the CLI and run it in a loop until all tasks are complete, with a stop hook and a max iteration count in Anthropic's plugin.

infographic.alt: Goal loop card (agent-native pattern). What it does: Keep working until a stated condition is met. In Claude Code: /goal and Stop hook continuation. What is new: A model judges the goal, so make it checkable.

anti_patterns.name: Prompt as enforcement
anti_patterns.symptom: A must-never rule lives only in CLAUDE.md or a system prompt.
anti_patterns.fix: Deterministic gate: a PreToolUse hook with onFailure: "block", or a deny rule, with a test.

anti_patterns.name: Context flooding
anti_patterns.symptom: Workers return full transcripts or logs to the coordinating thread.
anti_patterns.fix: Context isolation: ask each worker for a bounded final report.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded loop
anti_patterns.symptom: An automated run has no turn, cost, or depth limit.
anti_patterns.fix: Bounded execution on every layer: --max-turns, --max-budget-usd with headroom, maxTurns, spawn depth.

anti_patterns.name: Unverified done
anti_patterns.symptom: The agent declares success without running a check, or stops early.
anti_patterns.fix: Evaluator-optimizer with a real test, enforced by a Stop hook.

anti_patterns.name: Step repetition
anti_patterns.symptom: The agent redoes completed steps after an interruption or a reset of the conversation.
anti_patterns.fix: Durable progress outside the context (a task list or a file) and idempotent side effects.

anti_patterns.name: Rewind as rollback
anti_patterns.symptom: A team counts on /rewind to undo shell commands or remote effects.
anti_patterns.fix: Saga thinking: git commits before risky work, a written compensation for each external effect.

anti_patterns.name: Ordered hooks assumption
anti_patterns.symptom: A hook relies on another hook for the same event having run first.
anti_patterns.fix: Independent observers: each hook passes or blocks on its own.

anti_patterns.name: Specific allow overrides deny
anti_patterns.symptom: A narrow allow rule is added to punch a hole in a broad deny.
anti_patterns.fix: Permission rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow: narrow the deny instead.

anti_patterns.name: Unguarded shared checkout
anti_patterns.symptom: Parallel write-capable agents edit the same working tree.
anti_patterns.fix: Bulkhead: isolation: worktree per writing agent.

anti_patterns.name: Untrusted content as instructions
anti_patterns.symptom: Fetched pages, issue text, or tool output are allowed to steer the agent's next action.
anti_patterns.fix: Trust boundary: treat external content as data, and keep write and network tools behind permission rules.

further_reading.note: April 19, 2026. A catalog of harness practices: Git as durable state, compaction, skills with progressive disclosure, hooks as the enforcement layer, planner, generator and evaluator splits, and turning each agent mistake into a permanent rule.
April 2, 2026. A mental model of feedforward guides and feedback sensors, each computational or inferential, with a human steering the loop.
A guide of practical patterns for coding agents: subagents, red/green TDD, running the tests first, manual testing and anti-patterns.
March 2024. The four agentic design patterns that popularized the term: reflection, tool use, planning and multi-agent collaboration.
January 2025. Tool use, planning and plan validation, reflection, failure modes and agent evaluation.
June 2023. The planning, memory and tool-use decomposition that most later catalogs start from.
An MIT-licensed Agent Skill for designing and auditing harnesses, built on one rule: the model proposes actions, the harness validates, authorizes, executes and records them.
An MIT-licensed reading hub on orchestration, context and memory, tools and protocols, evaluation and production safety.
MIT-licensed, small runnable Python implementations of workflow patterns such as chaining, routing, parallelization, reflection and planning.
